source.author: verg
source.text: At levem clipeum sublatis cornibus Io auro insignibat, iam saetis obsita, iam bos argumentum ingens, et custos virginis Argus caelataque amnem fundens pater Inachus urna.
source.text_original: At levem clipeum sublatis cornibus Io / auro insignibat, iam saetis obsita, iam bos / (argumentum ingens), et custos virginis Argus / caelataque amnem fundens pater Inachus urna.
source.text_english: But Io was embossing the light shield with uplifted horns in gold, now shaggy with bristles, now a cow, a vast subject, and Argus, guardian of the maiden, and Inachus the father, pouring forth the river from a carved urn.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: eodem modo conuertisse in bouem traditur lo Inachi filiam, quae ut iram Iunonis effugeret, ut erat iam saetis obsita., iam bos, tranasse dicitur mare in Aegyptumque uenisse atque ibi recepta pristina specie dea facta quae nunc Isis uocatur.
reuse.text_original: eodem modo conuertisse in bouem traditur lo Inachi filiam, quae ut iram Iunonis effugeret, ut erat iam saetis obsita., iam bos, tranasse dicitur mare in Aegyptumque uenisse atque ibi recepta pristina specie dea facta quae nunc Isis uocatur.
reuse.text_english: In the same way the daughter of lo, namely Inachus, is said to have been turned into a cow; and, to escape the wrath of Juno, as she was already covered with bristles, now a cow, she is said to have crossed the sea and come into Egypt and there, having recovered her former form, to have been made a goddess, who is now called Isis.
